why_the_rule_landed_before_the_numbers: daedalus/mixture_opt.py trains nothing and reads no checkpoints, so every threshold in it is committed before a single arm has been scored. That ordering IS the deliverable -- the plan's standing rule is that thresholds are not tuned after seeing outcomes, and a rule arriving in the same commit as the numbers it judges is indistinguishable from one fitted to them. Constants: EXCESS_TEMPERATURE 0.10, EXCESS_RATIO_CAP 2.0, DOMAIN_FLOOR_FRACTION 0.4, QUALITY_HEAVY_RAW_SCALE 0.45, MAX_SOURCE_REGRESSION 0.05, MIN_AGGREGATE_GAIN 0.005.
excess_loss_is_defined_against_a_special: excess(s) = bpb_baseline(s) - bpb_specialist_s(s), where the specialist is the same tiny model on the same budget trained on s alone. That is what this architecture at this scale can do with that source; the gap is what the mixture leaves unclaimed. Every other reading of 'excess' needs a quantity nothing on this box measures -- a source's intrinsic entropy, or a reference model trained on data this program does not have. A negative excess is KEPT AS MEASURED, not clipped: a specialist re-reading a short source really can lose on that source's own holdout, and the honest consequence is that the rule down-weights it. The ratio cap is what stops one such number writing the mixture.
the_trap_that_would_have_decided_the_pha: train.py's in-run val_bpb weights the holdout by the mixture EACH RUN SAMPLES (Trainer._val_weights reads MixtureBatchSource.probs). Correct for a single run, and useless across arms: six models scored on six different corpora, subtractable-looking and meaningless. The comparison is scripts/bpb_eval.py under mixture_opt.evaluation_weights -- the baseline blueprint, the same for every arm -- and the sweep artifact carries those weights so a later pass can be checked for having used the same ones rather than assumed to have. val_bpb stays on as the divergence signal it is.
three_preflight_refusals_the_cap_flag_ca: summarize_mixture's capped_sources flags a source at or past the cap whether or not anything was reweighted, so it is not a usable guard. arm_preflight refuses, in order and all before the GPU is touched: (1) a source the arm names with no shards under the root -- resolve_mixture drops it and takes target_probs AFTER renormalizing, so this rewrite reports l1_skew_pts of exactly ZERO, and a baseline arm on a root that had lost stack-edu-python would train on web alone with a perfectly clean mixture summary; (2) l1_skew_pts > 1e-3, which is the cap water-filling one source's share onto the others; (3) max_epochs_seen >= 4.0, where the all-capped fallback PRESERVES the mixture and accepts repetition instead -- no skew to see, and an arm whose advantage could be a fourth pass over its own data is not evidence about mixtures.
measured_epochs_at_the_real_budget: baseline draws 0.25-0.26 epochs of each source; only-stack-edu-python draws 2.00 (100,000,000 tokens on disk against a 200,015,872 budget); only-fineweb-edu 0.47; only-dclm-baseline 0.77. Nothing is near the 4-epoch cap, so no arm is refused. The 2.0 on the code specialist is worth carrying into the report: a specialist is a BOUND on achievable BPB, and a more-repeated specialist is a slightly weaker bound, so code's excess loss is if anything understated.
